elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Company may also terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for any or no reason upon thirty (30) days advance written notice to Contractor". "For any or no reason" mirrors the retained §6(a) convenience formula and covers both the Agreement and the SOW (the Order Form analogue here). The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" fired false only because the insertion uses "for any or no reason" rather than the literal words "for convenience"; in substance the right is unconditional and unqualified.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days advance written notice to Contractor" — exactly 30 days and expressly written; no additional conditions (no SOW-completion precondition, no cure or approval gate).

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "in which case Contractor shall refund any prepaid fees pro rata for the period after the effective date of such termination" — the refund is expressly pro rata (not merely a post-termination-period refund) and is triggered by the new Company convenience right.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: "Contractor may not terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience while any Statement of Work is outstanding." The MSA has no fixed term; the only period of commitment is while a SOW is running, and Contractor is barred throughout it. This is consistent with retained §6(a), which already limits the mutual 15-day right to times when no uncompleted SOW is outstanding, so no retained sentence contradicts the bar.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted right runs on 30 days' notice, not 60–90 days. (Shorter notice is more favourable to Customer, but the fallback element is not literally met.)

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: neither the retained §6 nor the insertion imposes any early-termination fee or penalty on Company; §6(b)'s payment sentence covers only fees and expenses incurred/earned through the effective date, so there is no fee to cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Retained §6(a) lets Contractor terminate on 15 days' notice whenever no uncompleted SOW is outstanding; the effective date is not tied to the end of any term (and the MSA is indefinite, so no term-end anchor exists).

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Contractor's surviving §6(a) convenience right requires only "fifteen (15) days advance notice"; the insertion does not lengthen it.

reasons: All four preferred elements are met in operative language: a 30-day Company convenience right over the Agreement or any SOW, an express pro-rata prepaid-fee refund, and an express bar on Contractor convenience termination while any SOW is outstanding. The level is complete at preferred, so the fallback gaps (60–90 days, 90-day Vendor notice, term-end anchor) do not matter.

The failed regex "Customer convenience termination present" is a wording artifact: the insertion tracks the contract's own "for any or no reason" convenience formulation used in §6(a) rather than the phrase "for convenience". Substantively the right is unconditional and therefore a convenience right under the rule boundaries.

Minimality holds: two inserted sentences, no deletions, no removal of the Customer-favourable retained 15-day mutual right, and no extras (no "in whole or in part" surplus, no survival tail, no expense or procedure language, no damages or notice boilerplate). The Contractor bar is close to redundant with retained §6(a), but it is a direct implementation of a selected checklist element and additionally closes SOW-level convenience termination, which §6(a) does not address, so it is not treated as duplicate coverage.

Intent is preserved: §6(a) (mutual 15-day right only when no SOW is outstanding) and §6(b) (material-breach termination, payment through effective date, assignment of works in progress) survive intact and do not contradict the new Company right, which is expressly additive ("may also"). No undefined terms or dangling cross-references are created; "Statement of Work" is a defined term and Paragraph 2's reference to Paragraph 6 still resolves.

Optional polish only, not defects: the drafter could use the words "for convenience" and "prepaid fees paid or payable" alignment, and could state that the refund is Contractor's sole obligation on such termination — none of these is required by the checklist and adding them would risk minimality.
